description:
Company Overview:

We are building Protege to solve the biggest unmet need in AI — getting access to the right training data. The process today is time intensive, incredibly expensive, and often ends in failure. The Protege platform facilitates the secure, efficient, and privacy-centric exchange of AI training data.

Solving AI’s data problem is a generational opportunity. We’re backed by world-class investors and already powering partnerships with some of the most ambitious teams in AI. The company that succeeds will be one of the largest in AI — and in tech.

We’re a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

The role

The Ingestion team owns how data gets from our partners into Protege. Health systems and other data owners send us EHR records, claims, clinical notes, and medical imaging in whatever shape their systems produce. Ingestion builds the pipelines that move that data in, checks it before and after it lands, and converts formats like FHIR and DICOM into something the rest of our platform can use. Everything we deliver to a customer starts here, so a problem we miss at ingest ends up in a customer’s hands.

You’ll lead with player coach mentality and intensity. You’ll lead a team of three engineers today (more as we continue to grow) and report to our Head of Engineering. You’ll set technical direction, manage and grow the team, and spend about 25 to 40 percent of your week writing and reviewing code. Your closest partners are the team’s product manager and our forward-deployed engineers, who run ingests for specific partners and deals on the platform your team builds. The hard part is that every partner’s data is different and the volumes are large, while customer deals fix the delivery dates. Your job is to turn what we learn from each partner into checks and tooling, so the next one is faster and fewer problems reach customers.

What you'll do

  • Lead the team. Manage engineers: run planning, give feedback, coach, and hire as the team grows.

  • Own the ingestion platform. Our data transfer service, partner setup, and ingestion pipelines are reliable, and adding a new partner gets easier each time.

  • Finish and extend automated QA. Every new dataset is checked before and after ingest, and failures stop bad data before it moves downstream.

  • Add new formats and modalities. Adapters for FHIR, DICOM, and whatever a partner sends next are tested and reusable, not written once per partner.

  • Write and review code. You stay hands-on and set the standard for design and code review on the team.

  • Plan with Product and forward-deployed engineering. Agree on a roadmap, weigh platform work and technical debt against deal deadlines, and say early when a date is at risk.

What success looks like

  • 30 days: Learned the ingestion pipeline and QA framework, met Product, FDE, and the neighboring teams, took over standups, planning, and 1:1s, and merged a first change of your own.

  • 60 days: Owning the Ingestion roadmap and the automated QA rollout end to end, with a plan agreed with Product.

  • 90 days: Shipped the first milestone on that roadmap, with results you can point to: a new partner’s data came in faster than the last one did, and a problem that used to reach customers is now caught at ingest.

What you'll bring

  • Track record of hiring, onboarding and developing top engineering talent, while staying hands-on in the code.

  • Designed and shipped production systems end to end, and owned them after launch.

  • Built data pipelines or data-heavy backend systems that run at scale.

  • Made architecture trade-offs between speed, quality, and technical debt, and can explain the reasoning.

  • Planned and prioritized work with product managers and non-technical partners.

  • Hired, onboarded, and developed engineers.

  • Communicated clearly in a fast-moving environment with little process.

  • Nice to have: Built automated data validation or quality checks.

  • Nice to have: Worked with healthcare data or other regulated data.
